census.provenance_text:
# KEN-2334 github skill usage census (control host)

Collected read-only on the control VM on 2026-10-01 about 01:40Z (2026-09-30 evening local). Claude overseer sessions and subagents, Codex sessions and the closed-lane archives were read as streams. No GitHub API request, Linear write, archive extraction or git state change was made.

## Result in brief

- 255 executed `github.sh` commands were counted in 436 Claude transcripts and 8 Codex sessions of the kendex checkout. Every one ran on the control host.
- `pr-threads` is 182 of 255 calls (71.4%). With `pr-merge` the two verbs reach 83.9%. Eleven of the 24 advertised verbs were observed. Thirteen have zero executed calls.
- Lane calls are NOT measured. No lane session transcript survives in the closed-lane archives. The lane column holds 0 as "unmeasured", not "observed zero".
- Plain `gh` ran 1605 times in the same transcripts, about 6.3 times the `github.sh` count. `gh pr view` (with or without readiness fields), CI status reads and merge queue reads lead.
- The four waiters were barely run by hand on the control host (2 `queue-wait` calls, none for the others). Their archive prose mentions are proxies only.

## Evidence


## How calls were counted

- A call is a tool_use whose Bash `command` (or Codex `cmd:` literal) runs `github.sh` as a command word, optionally after `env`, `bash`, `timeout`, a variable alias, `-C PATH`, a loop keyword or a command substitution. The verb is the first word after `-C PATH`.
- Greps, cats, quoted prose, heredoc bodies, commit messages and mail text that merely name the script are not calls. Of 289 commands that contained the script name, 4 more ran it through `env -u` and were added after a recall check. The rest were reads or prose.
- Each command in a batch counts once. A shell loop counts once (no execution log proves iterations).
- Failure is the Claude tool_result `is_error` flag, which is the whole command's exit status. A pipe to `head` hides a script failure, so failed counts are lower bounds. A failure is attributed only when the command ran one counted invocation. Failures in multi-invocation commands: not attributed (1 failed `github.sh` commands in all). Codex batches and 12 calls without a stored result carry no failure value.
- A retry is a call with the same session, verb and arguments as the previous such call, where the previous call failed (attributable failures only).
- Items are distinct PR numbers or thread ids in the first positional argument. They are not mapped to KEN work items.
- Overseer column: Claude sessions titled overseer and their subagents, plus Codex sessions on the kendex checkout (the Codex overseer run and its helpers on 2026-09-27). Other control-host column: the two untitled Claude sessions in the kendex project. Lane column: 0, unmeasured.
- Two `pr-merge` calls aimed at `-C /home/admin/dev/hyprtrade` were dropped as another repository.

## Verb ranking (github.sh, all 24 advertised verbs)

Advertised table: `.agents/skills/github/SKILL.md` and `github.sh --help` list the same 24 verbs. Share and cumulative share use 255 deduplicated executed calls. Rows with 0 calls carry no rank.


Sources split (calls): Claude overseer top-level 225, Claude overseer subagents 4, Codex overseer 12, Claude other top-level 13, Claude other subagent 1.

## Related consumers (not github.sh calls)

Direct control-host invocations only. Proxy columns count mentions in prose (lane-mail, status files, workflow state; fleet_log rows), not runs.


## Wrapper scripts that call github.sh internally

Their inner `github.sh` calls are invisible in transcripts, so the ranking above undercounts verbs these scripts use. Counts are invocations from the same kendex-scope transcripts.


## Plain gh and gh api by equivalent github.sh verb

Executed `gh` commands in the kendex-scope transcripts: 1605 counted here, plus 85 aimed at other repositories (dropped). "no equivalent" means no advertised verb reads or writes that thing. Mapping is by sub-command and by endpoint or GraphQL text, so it is an approximation.


Top plain `gh` sub-commands before mapping: pr view 612, api graphql 227, run view 155, run list 103, pr list 85, pr checks 73, pr merge 27, pr diff 26, issue view 16, api repos/vanillagreencom/kendex/commits/$h/check-runs?per_page=100 14, api repos/vanillagreencom/kendex/commits/$h/status 11, pr edit 10.

## Excluded counts (other projects, not kendex)

github.sh / gh / wrapper / waiter commands found in other projects' control-host sessions, left out of every table above: fleet Claude sessions 123 github.sh, 1211 gh, 8 waiter; vg 55 github.sh, 289 gh; talk 2 github.sh, 120 gh; fleet Codex sessions 7 github.sh, 15 gh. These repositories carry their own checkouts, so their calls do not measure kendex work.

## Limits for the reader

- The lane side of the workload is the largest gap. Lanes run the PR phase (create, wait, thread reply and resolve, merge arm). Their `pr-create`, `post-reply`, `resolve-thread`, `pr-edit-body`, label and CI-log use is unmeasured, and the 0 rows for those verbs mean "not seen on the control host".
- Prose proxies (archive and fleet_log columns) show that lane mail names `pr-merge`, `queue-wait`, `approval-wait`, `ci-wait` and `pr-watch.sh` often. Mentions are not executions.
- The `github.sh` count excludes the work wrapper scripts do. A keep, slim or drop decision for a verb that a wrapper calls should not read a low count here as low use.

Evidence.value: executed tool-call records (Claude assistant `tool_use` entries with Bash `command`; Codex `exec` custom-tool calls with each `cmd:` literal). Not workflow-state or prose proxies. Proxies sit in their own columns.

(5) Calls made inside wrapper scripts (see wrapper table) leave no tool record and are not counted.

The plan's `/home/dev/dev/kendex` is `/home/admin/dev/kendex`. The plan's `/home/dev/dev/.worktrees/kendex` is `/home/admin/dev/.worktrees/kendex` (absent). The plan's `/home/dev/.fleet/archive/kendex` is `/home/admin/.fleet/archive/kendex`.

Cross-check only, not a call-count source. expectedHeadSha.description: The expected SHA of the pull request's HEAD ref

after.description: Cursor for pagination, used only by the get_review_comments method. Pass the endCursor from the previous page's PageInfo to fetch the next page.

method.description:
Action to specify what pull request data needs to be retrieved from GitHub. 
Possible options: 
 1. get - Get details of a specific pull request.
 2. get_diff - Get the diff of a pull request.
 3. get_status - Get combined commit status of a head commit in a pull request.
 4. get_files - Get the list of files changed in a pull request. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 5. get_commits - Get the list of commits on a pull request. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 6. get_review_comments - Get review threads on a pull request. Each thread contains logically grouped review comments made on the same code location during pull request reviews. Returns thread metadata and comments with nullable current and original line-range coordinates (line, start_line, original_line, original_start_line). Current coordinates are omitted when unavailable, such as for outdated comments. Use cursor-based pagination (perPage, after) to control results.
 7. get_reviews - Get the reviews on a pull request. When asked for review comments, use get_review_comments method. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 8. get_comments - Get comments on a pull request. Use this if user doesn't specifically want review comments. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 9. get_check_runs - Get check runs for the head commit of a pull request. Check runs are the individual CI/CD jobs and checks that run on the PR.

perPage.description: Results per page for pagination (min 1, max 100)

method.description: The write operation to perform on pull request review.

threadId.description: The node ID of the review thread (e.g., PRRT_kwDOxxx). Required for resolve_thread and unresolve_thread methods. Get thread IDs from pull_request_read with method get_review_comments.

actor_name.description: The handle for the GitHub user account to filter rule suites on. Used by the 'list_rule_suites' method.

branch.description: Branch name. Required for the 'get_rules_for_branch' method.

enterprise.description: Enterprise slug. Required when level is 'enterprise'.

evaluate_status.description: Filter rule suites by ruleset evaluation mode. Used by the 'list_rule_suites' method.

includes_parents.description: Include rulesets configured at higher levels that also apply. Defaults to true. Used by the 'get' and 'list' methods at the repository level.

level.description:
The level at which the ruleset is configured:
- 'repository': A ruleset on a single repository (requires 'owner' and 'repo').
- 'organization': A ruleset covering repositories in an organization (requires 'org').
- 'enterprise': A ruleset covering repositories across an enterprise (requires 'enterprise').

method.description:
Operation to perform:
- 'get': Get a specific ruleset by ID (requires 'ruleset_id'). Supported at every level.
- 'list': List all rulesets. Supported at every level.
- 'get_rules_for_branch': Get all rules that apply to a branch (requires 'branch'). Repository level only.
- 'list_rule_suites': List rule suites, the evaluations of rules against pushes. Repository and organization levels only.
- 'get_rule_suite': Get a specific rule suite by ID (requires 'rule_suite_id'). Repository and organization levels only.

org.description: Organization name. Required when level is 'organization'.

owner.description: Repository owner. Required when level is 'repository'.

perPage.description: Results per page for pagination (min 1, max 100)

ref.description: The name of the ref (branch, tag, etc.) to filter rule suites by. Used by the 'list_rule_suites' method.

repo.description: Repository name. Required when level is 'repository'.

repository_name.description: Repository name to filter rule suites by. Used by the 'list_rule_suites' method at the organization level.

rule_suite_id.description: Rule suite ID. Required for the 'get_rule_suite' method.

rule_suite_result.description: The rule suite result to filter by. Used by the 'list_rule_suites' method.

ruleset_id.description: Ruleset ID. Required for the 'get' method.

time_period.description: The time period to filter rule suites by. Used by the 'list_rule_suites' method.
